PAPERS.short: Zhang US wildfire smoke five-year mortality impulse response 2026
PAPERS.title: Wildfire smoke leaves a large five-year imprint on mortality in the United States
PAPERS.pm: Monthly county-level wildfire-attributable PM2.5 (smoke PM2.5 surface)
PAPERS.n: County-month mortality and wildfire-PM2.5 panels 2011-2023; episodic smoke pulses are used to deconvolve overlapping responses and recover an impulse-response function. Excess mortality peaks about three years after a pulse and is gone by five. Integrated over 2011-2023 this gives 1.7 million smoke-associated deaths (95% UI 1.1-2.3 million), roughly ten times what long-term ambient PM2.5 relative risks imply; circulatory and respiratory causes contribute comparably, adults >=65 dominate, and responses were larger during COVID-19. Limitation: a three-year lag in an ecological panel is exposed to slow confounders (migration, economic shocks, drought, heat) co-varying with fire years; the order-of-magnitude excess needs independent replication before it enters burden accounting. Relevance: high - a multi-year lag makes historical smoke-PM2.5 reconstructions, including LCS-corrected ones, the binding input.

PAPERS.short: Chyzhykov gravimetric filter water Karl Fischer bias 2026
PAPERS.title: Impact of Mass Loading and Water Speciation on Precision and Artifacts in Gravimetric Measurements of Atmospheric Particulate Matter
PAPERS.pm: Gravimetric PM1, PM2.5, PM10 on 47 mm glass-fibre filters; Karl Fischer coulometric filter water
PAPERS.n: Thirty filters (n=5 per fraction per site) plus five field blanks, weighed under PN-EN 12341:2024 conditioning, then stepwise thermal water release at 50, 120, 180 and 250 C. Between-filter variability was U-shaped in mass loading, minimal near 1330-1360 ug; PM1 was the most variable fraction (CV up to 53%). Strongly bound water (180-250 C) made up 51-60% of filter water, survives standard conditioning, and adds a systematic +3% to +18% mass bias, largest for PM1 at the steelworks. Limitation: 35 filters at two industrial sites; the bias is not yet resolved by composition or RH history, so transfer to urban background aerosol is untested. Relevance: high - every LCS calibration inherits the reference's error; a positive, composition-dependent water bias in gravimetric PM1 and PM2.5 propagates directly into co-location slopes.

PAPERS.title: Air pollution exposure and cataract outcomes: a systematic review and pollutant-specific meta-analysis
PAPERS.pm: Long-term PM2.5, PM10, NO2, black carbon (study-specific models)
PAPERS.n: Fifteen observational studies, seven pooled with REML random effects (search to 10 Aug 2026; ROBINS-E). PM2.5: HR 1.036 (0.988-1.086) per 1 ug/m3, I2 99.7%; NO2: HR 1.041 (1.013-1.070) per 10 ug/m3, I2 86%; black carbon per IQR: HR 1.010 (0.983-1.038), I2 33%. Highest-vs-lowest quartile was positive for NO2 (HR 1.094, 1.057-1.133) and null for PM2.5 and PM10; Knapp-Hartung widened the NO2 interval. Limitation: with I2 near 100% the pooled PM2.5 point estimate is not interpretable as a common effect - it averages incompatible exposure models and outcome definitions across too few studies. Relevance: low-moderate - the NO2 > PM2.5 ordering points at traffic proximity, which a dense network resolves better than satellite PM2.5.

PAPERS.short: Lu PM2.5 longevity country panel specification analysis 2026
PAPERS.title: Paradoxical PM2.5-longevity estimates in global country panels are sensitive to differential trend control: a specification analysis, 2000-2023
PAPERS.pm: Population-weighted annual ambient PM2.5 (World Bank WDI)
PAPERS.n: 4,406 country-years, two-way fixed effects with GDP, health spending and urbanisation. The conventional model gives a paradoxical +0.406 y life expectancy per 10 ug/m3 PM2.5 (0.144-0.668); economy-specific linear trends remove it (-0.023 y, -0.175 to 0.129), as do first differences (-0.006 y, -0.085 to 0.073). A future-exposure lead (+2 y) was positive alone (0.296, 0.042-0.549) but attenuated with current exposure. Limitation: the trend-adjusted estimates are null rather than negative, so the paper diagnoses bias without recovering the expected harm; national averaging discards almost all exposure contrast. Relevance: moderate - a methods warning for any ecological PM2.5 panel, including those fed by sensor-network or satellite exposure surfaces.

PAPERS.short: Ni Wuhan birth cohort air pollution neurodevelopment target trial 2026
PAPERS.title: Early Life Ambient Air Pollution, Sex Steroids and Neurodevelopment: Target Trial Emulation in a Prospective Cohort
PAPERS.pm: Residential ambient pollutants (PM and gases) from preconception to age 2
PAPERS.endpoint: Bayley MDI and PDI at age 2; cord-serum sex steroids
PAPERS.n: 3,575 mother-child pairs (2014-2019), cord sex steroids in 897. Most pollutants were inversely associated with Bayley scores across windows, strongest in the first postnatal year. Androstenedione mediated 5-12% of some preconception/prenatal associations with PDI, but the IPW indirect effects lost significance. Target trial emulation of China's 2013-2017 Action Plan: children in the later policy period scored 7.27 (MDI) and 6.41 (PDI) points higher. Limitation: the policy contrast is a birth-period comparison, so secular changes in Bayley administration, parental education and care confound it; per-pollutant effect sizes and CIs are not in the abstract. Relevance: moderate - the postnatal window being most sensitive argues for exposure assigned to the infant's home, where indoor low-cost monitors outperform residential-grid estimates.

PAPERS.short: Kalisa East Africa passive sampler network PAHs metals 2026
PAPERS.title: First Results from a Passive Air Monitoring Network across Five East African Countries for Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) and Metals
PAPERS.pm: PUF passive samplers: 23 PAHs, 24 trace metals (total and water-soluble)
PAPERS.geo: East Africa (five countries, 10 sites incl. Bukavu)
PAPERS.n: Ten sites, 30-day dry-season deployments everywhere and paired wet-season samples at four. PAH ring profiles and metal loadings were spatially heterogeneous; water-soluble metals were a small share of total. HYSPLIT put >90% of air masses from the S-SE, and adjacent cross-border sites saw near-identical air, so concentration differences are local-source driven; PCA components explained 46.5% and 19.9% of variance. Wet-season levels were lower. Screening risk was metal-dominated at some sites and PAH-dominated at Bukavu. Limitation: PUF-PAS uptake rates for particle-bound species are uncertain and site-specific, so concentrations are semi-quantitative; no PM mass. Relevance: high - electricity-free composition sampling is the natural complement to optical LCS mass networks in data-sparse Africa.

PAPERS.short: Simkovich LPG stove RCT quality of life 2026
PAPERS.title: Cooking With Liquefied Petroleum Gas or Biomass and Quality of Life: Results From a Randomized Controlled Trial
PAPERS.n: 180 women primary cooks aged 25-64 randomised to an LPG stove, 12 months of free fuel and behavioural reinforcement vs usual cooking; 179 completed. ITT at 12 months: SF-36 mental 48.3 vs 50.9 (p=0.59), physical 53.1 vs 47.6 (p=0.08), EQ-5D VAS 67.0 vs 71.7 (p=0.05); no personal PM2.5-QOL exposure-response. More intervention women felt financially better off (42% vs 13%) and reported higher income (33% vs 9%), both p<0.001. Limitation: QOL is a secondary outcome in a trial powered for something else, unblinded, and the fuel subsidy itself transfers income, so the financial result is partly mechanical. Relevance: moderate - personal PM2.5 monitoring was available but the QOL signal was absent; intervention trials remain the strongest design for testing whether measured reductions matter.

PAPERS.short: Edwards macrophage superoxide SOA biomass plastic burning PM 2026
PAPERS.title: Superoxide Release from Macrophages upon Exposure to Secondary Organic Aerosols, Biomass, and Plastic Burning Particulate Matter
PAPERS.pm: Laboratory SOA (limonene, toluene, naphthalene), biomass- and plastic-burning PM suspensions
PAPERS.n: Macrophages exposed to PM suspensions, superoxide followed for 4 h by chemiluminescence plus EPR; an activation threshold is defined as the dose of a clear superoxide rise. Limonene SOA gave the largest release (~32 uM) but the highest threshold (300 ug/mL); naphthalene and toluene SOA gave 2.5-7 uM with thresholds of 0.02-0.1 ug/mL. Biomass PM had no clear threshold. Plastic-burning PM ranged widely: PET highest output (~12 uM), PS/LDPE/HDPE thresholds ~0.01 ug/mL, PVC and PET 50-100 ug/mL. Limitation: suspension doses in ug/mL do not map onto deposited alveolar doses, and a single cell line under submerged exposure omits surfactant and epithelial interaction. Relevance: moderate - per-mass oxidative potency varies by four orders of magnitude across sources, which mass-only sensors cannot register.

PAPERS.short: Sittitoon Thailand haze PM2.5 symptoms inequality 2026
PAPERS.title: Health inequalities in PM2.5-related symptoms during Thailand's haze season: the role of education, sociodemographic, lifestyle, protective behaviors, and environmental factors
PAPERS.pm: Provincial monthly PM2.5 from satellite-based products
PAPERS.endpoint: Acute respiratory, eye, skin and neurological symptoms
PAPERS.n: 3,916 adults interviewed January-April 2025, mixed-effects logistic models with latent-class protective-behaviour phenotypes. Symptom prevalence: respiratory 80.7%, eye 52.8%, skin 48.7%, neurological 33.1%. Higher provincial PM2.5 was independently associated with respiratory and dermatological symptoms; non-compliers (48.6%) and the neutral group had higher odds of respiratory and neurological symptoms than compliers (33.4%). Female sex, younger age, comorbidity, alcohol, urban residence and lack of village-health-volunteer contact also raised risk. Limitation: one satellite value per province per month is assigned to every respondent, so the PM2.5 contrast is between-province and confounded with region; self-reported symptoms during a publicised haze season invite reporting bias; odds ratios are not given in the abstract. Relevance: high - northern Thailand has dense low-cost networks that could replace provincial satellite means with district-level exposure.

PAPERS.short: Huang gut microbiota mediation air pollution metabolic syndrome 2026
PAPERS.title: The mediating roles of gut microbiota in the associations of air pollution and meteorological factors with metabolic syndrome
PAPERS.pm: Long-term residential PM2.5 and NO2; ambient temperature
PAPERS.n: Gut microbial community clusters were derived and related to metabolic syndrome; health-associated clusters were dominated by Bacteroides and Prevotella. Long-term NO2, PM2.5 and temperature were associated with microbiota composition, and Megamonas and Megasphaera statistically mediated their associations with MetS. The abstract reports no sample size, effect estimates, mediated proportions or confidence intervals. Limitation: mediation from a single stool sample assumes exposure precedes the microbiome state and that diet, a strong common cause of both microbiota and MetS, is adequately adjusted - neither can be checked from the record. Relevance: low - mechanistic hypothesis generation; exposure resolution is not the limiting factor here.

PAPERS.short: Yoon PRL-3 ezrin airway epithelium particulate matter 2026
PAPERS.title: PRL-3-sensitive cytoskeletal signaling mediates early airway epithelial responses to particulate matter
PAPERS.pm: Urban PM (UPM), diesel exhaust particles, PM10 reference materials
PAPERS.n: Phosphoproteomics of human bronchial epithelial cells under non-cytotoxic PM exposure, with pharmacological and genetic PRL-3 (PTP4A3) suppression and an acute mouse airway exposure model. PM rapidly and transiently upregulated PRL-3 and relocalised it to the membrane, with PRL-3-sensitive ezrin dephosphorylation in vitro and in vivo. Blocking PRL-3 restored ezrin phosphorylation and attenuated EMT-associated changes and MUC5AC upregulation, independent of Akt, ERK and mTOR, and reproducibly across UPM, DEP and PM10. Limitation: doses are described as non-lethal but not related to deposited human doses; acute exposure says nothing about chronic remodelling. Relevance: low for sensing - a candidate early-effect pathway shared across PM types, i.e. not composition-specific.

PAPERS.short: Pourkiaei Santiago CMAQ EDGAR vs INEMA inventories 2026
PAPERS.title: High-Resolution Air Quality Modeling over Santiago, Chile: A Comparative Assessment of EDGAR and INEMA Anthropogenic Emission Inventories
PAPERS.pm: CMAQ PM2.5 (9/3/1 km nests), source apportionment and DDM sensitivities
PAPERS.n: Global EDGAR v8.1 (2022) vs regional INEMA v2 (2020) in CMAQ with three one-way nests to 1 km. Aggregate PM2.5 emissions were similar but sectoral splits differed sharply; INEMA reproduced PM better, EDGAR daytime O3. After scaling emissions to mean observations, source apportionment shifted between industrial combustion (EDGAR) and transport (INEMA), with building energy use important in both. DDM showed VOC-limited O3 and sector-specific non-linear second-order PM2.5 sensitivity to NOx. Limitation: calibrating emissions to the observed mean forces agreement and then attributes sources within that constrained state, so apportionment differences reflect inventory structure, not validated truth; performance statistics are not in the abstract. Relevance: moderate - 1 km CTM fields are the prior that dense LCS networks are fused with in Andean basins.

PAPERS.short: Qian MAG-MISD probabilistic multi-station PM2.5 forecasting 2026
PAPERS.title: MAG-MISD: A Mode-Specific Adaptive Graph Framework for Multiscale Interaction and Station Dependence in Probabilistic PM2.5 Forecasting
PAPERS.pm: Hourly station PM2.5, 127 Yangtze River Delta monitors, 8 years
PAPERS.n: Variational mode decomposition into five components, cross-mode Transformer per station, and a separate directed graph per mode (geographic, persistent adaptive and sample-conditioned dynamic edges) before fusion into conditional quantiles. Against the same-input VMD-iTransformer, RMSE fell 4.76%, 2.78%, 0.13% and 0.72% at 1, 6, 12 and 24 h, with better pinball loss and interval score and ~70% fewer parameters; the persistent adaptive relation drove most of the gain in ablation. Limitation: the improvement vanishes beyond 6 h, and decomposition of the full series before splitting risks leakage unless done causally - the abstract does not say. Relevance: moderate - station-graph forecasting transfers to LCS networks, where per-mode dependence could also flag drifting nodes.

PAPERS.short: Ghazaryan explainable ML annual PM2.5 Europe Central Asia 2026
PAPERS.title: Explainable Machine Learning for PM2.5 Prediction and Comparative Country-Level Risk Assessment in Europe and Central Asia
PAPERS.pm: Annual city PM2.5 vs climatic and socio-economic indicators
PAPERS.n: Fifty-nine country-year observations (ten cities, 2020-2025) with eleven predictors; six models under five-fold CV. Linear regression had the lowest RMSE and highest R2, Extra Trees the lowest MAE; SHAP attributed added information to development indicators beyond meteorology. The authors call the result exploratory. Limitation: 59 observations and 11 predictors with random-fold CV on autocorrelated city panels cannot support model ranking or attribution; numeric skill is not reported in the abstract. Relevance: low - illustrates why annual aggregate predictors are no substitute for measured spatial coverage.

PAPERS.short: Dahl air pollution bone fractures high-risk population 2026
PAPERS.title: Air pollution and bone fractures in a high-risk population: differences by age and sex
PAPERS.pm: Ambient air pollution (metric not stated in record)
PAPERS.n: No abstract at harvest. The title indicates an analysis of ambient air pollution and fracture risk in a population at high fracture risk, stratified by age and sex. Recorded for coverage; no exposure model, design or estimate is inferred. Relevance: low-moderate - fracture is an under-studied PM endpoint, and bone-health associations have so far rested on residential annual means.
